Subject: POC trial: model selection + success criteria (post-call recap)

Hi Sara / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC kickstarted: 

Summary of ask
- Prototype an assistant that can answer clinical policy questions from internal docs and route more complex questions to a human.
- Must support English + Spanish (primary), French (secondary).

Proposed POC scope (see attached poc_scope.xlsx)
- 4-week hands-on trial: week 0 = kickoff & dataset ingestion; weeks 1-3 = evaluation, tuning; week 4 = handoff and exec demo.
- Deliverables: integration guide, evaluation results, recommended model config and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Success criteria (proposed)
- 95th percentile response latency < 300ms for single-turn queries (target: <200ms if feasible)
- Retrieval+generation accuracy: automated precision@k >= 0.75 on labeled eval set and human QA score >= 4/5 on 50 sampled queries
- No PII leakage in results; SOC2-aligned evidence provided

Ownership / next steps
- Redwood: Aditya (SE) will lead model selection & eval plan; Dev (engineer) will help with integration steps.
- Acme Health: Sara/Tom to provide initial eval dataset + a short list of 50 representative queries by Tue 17 Mar.
- Marissa (me) will set up kickoff meeting once we confirm timeline.

Model asks we discussed (high level)
- You mentioned cost sensitivity and desire for predictability. For the trial we'll propose an open-model first pass and a lower-cost fallback. Aditya will share specifics.

Attachments: poc_scope.xlsx, evaluation_dataset_template.csv (templates)

Can you confirm timelines and the person who will own the eval dataset? Once confirmed I'll send a calendar invite for the kickoff.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligned to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: we have a small internal compliance window the week of 23 Mar, so could we aim for a 6-week trial instead of 4 (kickoff the week of 23 Mar)? That gives us time to pull together the eval dataset and legal review.
- Success criteria: precision@k is good; additionally we care about hallucination rate on clinical guidance (we'll provide a labeled set to measure that). Human QA score target is fine.
- Multilingual: English + Spanish are musts. French is desirable but can be a stretch goal. We expect some code-switching examples in Spanish (medical terms in English).

Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection + success criteria (post-call recap)

Sara — thanks for the clarifications. Below is a pragmatic model selection + evaluation plan tailored to your constraints (cost sensitivity + multilingual needs).

1) Recommended model strategy for the POC- Primary (quality, English-first): Llama 2 13B (chat-tuned) quantized to q4_K_M or q8_0 depending on latency trials. This balances generation quality and moderate GPU memory footprint.
- Why: strong instruction-following and good performance on domain Q&A when combined with retrieval.

- Fallback (cost/latency / low-cost option): Mistral 7B Instruct quantized (q4_K_M). Lower compute cost and typically lower latency on the same infra; acceptable quality for many prompts and helpful as a baseline.

- Multilingual: BLOOMZ 7B (or M2M-100 for heavy translation coverage) for Spanish/French; workflow: run retrieval + prompt in original language against multilingual index and use BLOOMZ for generation, or use Llama 2 for English-heavy queries and BLOOMZ for Spanish/French. We can prototype both approaches early in the POC.

2) Evaluation plan (what we'll measure)- Automated: precision@k on your labeled set, F1 where applicable, hallucination rate (false assertions relative to references), and token/response latency distribution (p50/p95).
- Human QA: 50 sampled queries reviewed by clinical SME for correctness, safety, and clarity (score 1-5).

3) Technical constraints & config recommendations- Response latency target: aim p95 < 300ms for single-turn on dedicated instance shapes; if we need p95 <200ms we may need to use smaller quantized variants or dedicated GPU footprint (we'll quantify in week 0).
- Suggested runtime: start with continuous batching disabled for latency-sensitive queries; enable KV caching for multi-turn flows in later stages.

4) Ownership & runbook
- Aditya: model configs, eval harness, and run comparisons (Llama2 vs Mistral vs BLOOMZ).
- Dev: integration points for retrieval and dataset ingestion; will share a short integration checklist.

5) Deliverables and timeline (adjusted for 6 weeks)
- Week 0 (kickoff): dataset handoff, infra choices, initial model spin-up.
- Weeks 1-3: automated eval runs, iterate prompts/configs.
- Weeks 4-5: human QA and tuning.
- Week 6: final report, cost/latency profiling, and exec demo.

6) Security items
- We'll attach a SOC2 one-pager and a POC data handling checklist. During the POC we provide access logs, prompt logs (redacted as needed), and model versioning records.

I'll prepare a simple script to run a side-by-side eval of the three model paths (Llama2, Mistral, BLOOMZ) against your sample set; should have initial numbers by end of week 1.
